text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament finished its term on Tuesday.
- The old government has resigned and was empowered to continue its work until the new coalition of the Homeland Union and the Christian Democrats, holding 86 seats out of 141, forms a new cabinet.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas is considering whether or not to go to the summit of the three Baltic presidents in Riga next week, especially if Latvian Prime minister Andris Shkele attends the meeting, said a foreign ministry official, commenting on Shkele's reportedly offensive words quoted by Lithuanian newspaper Verslo Zinios.
- A record number of securities, 41 issues, was traded at the Lithuanian stock exchange session.
- Demand exceeded the supply of government T-bills by nearly three times at an auction of three-month paper. The average interest rate was 11.38 percent.

- The government approved a 510 million litas share issue for crisis-hit Innovation Bank. Temporary bank administrator Romualdas Visokavicius expects that the government will invest 390 million litas in the shares.

- The government abolished the restriction on foreigners controlling no more than 49 percent of oil terminal Klaipedos Nafta shares. This means it can sell 20-30 percent of its shares to local and foreign investors. Russian Jukos and Lukoil companies are mentioned among the potential investors.

- Parliament expressed its worry over developments in Belarus and urged President Alexander Lukashenko to respect democracy, the constitution and seek dialogue with parliament and other legal institutions.

- The coalition agreement between the Homeland Union and Christian Democratic parties is expected formally to be signed today. The coalition will have 86 seat in parliament, enough to form a new government.

- Lithuania needs to accumulate at least 480,000 tonnes of heating oil to ensure the normal functioning of the energy system before the start of next year, Energy Minister Saulius Kutas said. To reach the target Lithuania has to buy some 240,000 tonnes more of heating oil.
